page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-6xCPU-16GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 6 shared vCPUs mapped to 6 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system architecture is x86_64, with a CPU cache configuration of 64 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 16 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding 2.67 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it provides one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results show mixed performance characteristics. The shared CPU allocation results in poor single-core stress-ng performance of 787.9 and weak multi-core stress-ng performance of 4703.94. However, Geekbench testing indicates a strong single-core score of 2028.0 and a strong text processing score of 2628.0. Memory bandwidth read-only operations are average, measuring 616.67 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 43.56 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, though large block write bandwidth is weak at 24.88 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput is also weak at 5.86 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of this server is its shared CPU allocation, which limits sustained high-compute workloads but offers a cost-efficient resource density for non-intensive tasks. It performs adequately on standard operations, as shown by average scores in software compilation, ray tracing, and Redis SET operations which reach 8.81 million operations per second. It is suitable for general-purpose workloads, lightweight text processing, basic database operations, and small-scale LLM inference using models under 7B parameters, where prompt processing averages 655.67 tokens per second.

Performance benchmarks reveal a contrast between weak multi-core stress-ng results and strong Geekbench single-core and text processing scores.
